edited_for_packaging.why: This is the task's defect, not a packaging adjustment. The four-line `batch.non_tensor_batch["uid"] = ...` assignment (with its `# add uid to batch` comment) was moved verbatim from above `gen_batch = self._get_gen_batch(batch)` to below `batch = batch.union(gen_batch_output)`. Nothing else in the file changed: the move is a pure relocation, so the file still contains exactly one uid assignment in the training loop and exactly two `uuid.uuid4()` call sites overall, as upstream does.
edited_for_packaging.diff_shape: one 5-line deletion, one 5-line insertion, no other hunks

edited_for_packaging.action: packaging-adjusted after the first recording attempt
edited_for_packaging.why: Added verl's `file` tracking backend (trainer.logger gains "file"; VERL_FILE_LOGGER_PATH set next to LOG_FILE). The `console` backend prints metrics from inside the TaskRunner Ray actor, and Ray's forwarding of that stdout into the launch log proved nondeterministic on this image: attempt 1 wrote 0 `step:N` lines to the log while the Ray worker log held all 61; attempt 2 wrote all 61 to both. Without this the task could ship a frozen log with no metrics in it. The `file` backend writes unbuffered and does not involve Ray.
edited_for_packaging.behavioural_scope: logging only; no change to model, data, algorithm, batch sizes, step budget or seed

added_for_this_task.why: The launch script's 0/1 reward wrapper around math_dapo.compute_score. Not an upstream file; it belongs to this recipe and is shared with the sibling task. The 0/1 reward range is what makes the defect's advantage signature (min exactly 0.0, max exactly 1.0) legible.

added_for_this_task.why: Not an upstream file. Deliberate differences from the sibling, each chosen to remove a confounder or to shrink the run, are listed in deliberate_recipe_changes below.
Marks where the recorded run's log lands. Contains no task id, metric threshold, or defect hint.

deliberate_recipe_changes.why: 4 prompts per update at this model's ~3-10% base accuracy makes most GRPO groups all-incorrect; that is the sibling task's own second root cause and would be a confounder here. 8 prompts x 8 samples keeps mixed-reward groups common, so the healthy arm has a genuine non-degenerate group baseline to be destroyed.

The defect's signature is present from step 1 and does not need a long horizon: the advantage statistics are wrong on the first logged step. 60 steps with TEST_FREQ 20 still yields held-out points at steps 0, 20, 40, 60.
This task is issue-level only and is diagnosed from logged metrics; checkpoints would only add wall-clock and disk.

leak_audit.chosen_because: It names the recipe (DAPO-Math) and not the defect, unlike the sibling leaf task_monkey_patch_011 which names its own defect file.
leak_audit.experiment_name_placeholder: The launch script defaults EXPERIMENT_NAME to ${BENCH_TASK_LEAF_ID:-__BENCH_TASK_ID__}; no harness code sets BENCH_TASK_LEAF_ID, so a fresh run emits the literal __BENCH_TASK_ID__ and the recorded log stays free of the leaf id.
leak_audit.known_residual: The parent directory name verl_implementation states the defect class ('it is an implementation bug'). It is inherited from the existing family and does not reach the agent through the harness: TaskPackage.task_id is paths.root.name, so AUTORLBENCH_TASK_ID, the Harbor task name, the trial name and the compose project name all carry the leaf only. It must not be reintroduced into prepare.sh's header.
